facts.text: Father John Schoenmakers founded Osage Mission on April 28, 1847—seven years before Kansas became a territory—laying the groundwork for what would become St. Paul.
The Osage Catholic Mission, founded in St. Paul, stood as the most important frontier settlement in Southeast Kansas.
Francis Parish Cemetery preserves the Osage Mission’s history, including the lone surviving building of Mother Bridget Hayden’s girls’ school from 1847.
From about December 1862 to June 1865 Union soldiers were intermittently stationed at or near the mission.
The Osage Mission Infirmary & Guest House, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, operates today as St. Paul’s historic lodging.
St. Paul sits in Neosho County, Kansas, a small community shaped by its early mission roots.
